findings.title: Nil request dereference in ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods
findings.body: In `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` dereference `req.PluginContext` without checking whether `req` is `nil`. Previously, `MetricsMiddleware` (formerly `InstrumentationMiddleware`) ran before `instrumentContext` and failed early in `pluginTarget` when a plugin was not registered, whereas `LoggerMiddleware` explicitly guards against `req == nil` (lines 63, 77, 90, 104 of `logger_middleware.go`) and tests in `logger_middleware_test.go` exercise nil requests. If `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is invoked with a `nil` request (or if `req == nil` reaches it before any check), `req.PluginContext` will panic with a nil pointer dereference. Add a `if req == nil` check before calling `instrumentContext` in each of these methods.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new detached TestLogger, discarding recorded logs
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` (a fresh instance) rather than `f`. In `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest`, logging was changed from `m.logger.Info(...)` to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. Any test that passes a `*TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and then inspects `testLogger.InfoLogs` (such as existing tests in `logger_middleware_test.go`) will now see 0 calls because the `Info` call is recorded on the throwaway `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext` instead of on `f`. `FromContext` (and likely `New`) on `TestLogger` should return `f` so assertions on the injected test logger continue to work.
